Jerri Green

Democratic candidate for Governor, Tennessee · Open seat

Attorney; Memphis City Council member (District 2)

Jerri Green is a Memphis attorney who has represented District 2 on the Memphis City Council since winning a runoff in 2023. She was the Democratic nominee for Tennessee House District 83 in 2020. She won the Democratic primary for governor on August 6, 2026, and faces Republican nominee Marsha Blackburn and several independent candidates on November 3, 2026.

Where Green stands

Cost of living / Taxes
Proposes eliminating the state grocery tax and ending tax rebates to big businesses.
State budget / Social services
Proposes using unspent federal TANF (Temporary Assistance for Needy Families) funds to erase medical debt, waive housing security deposits and clear childcare waitlists. She also says the state should reconsider how much it keeps in its rainy day fund.
Abortion / Reproductive health
Says she would issue an executive order so doctors can provide women's healthcare without fear of prosecution under Tennessee's abortion laws.
Immigration enforcement
Supports ending the Tennessee Highway Patrol's cooperation with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
Education
Proposes appointing an education commissioner who has classroom experience. She opposes taking money out of public schools.
Economic development / Data centers
Proposes ending state incentives for data centers.
Criminal justice / Prisons
Proposes not renewing the state's private prison contracts.
Debates
Has repeatedly challenged Marsha Blackburn to a public debate, and agreed to take part in the Tennessee Press Association's Oct. 27 governor's forum.
